content.title: About
content.content: Haddock is a cold‑water marine fish of the cod family, found in the North Atlantic. Fried haddock is made from fillets that are breaded and deep‑fried until golden and crisp. It has a mild, slightly sweet flavor and a flaky texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Haddock is one of the most popular fish in the United Kingdom and Canada.
It provides more protein per calorie than most other seafood.
Wild haddock can grow up to 1 m, but commercial fillets usually come from fish 30–50 cm long.
Traditional dishes include “fish and chips” and smoked haddock (Finnan haddie).
Haddock migrates long distances during spawning, often traveling hundreds of kilometers.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: A 100 g serving of fried haddock supplies about 20 g of complete protein for muscle maintenance.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: When fried with a moderate amount of oil, haddock remains relatively low‑calorie compared with many meats.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Haddock is rich in vitamin B12, niacin and B6, which support nervous system function and energy metabolism.

items.title: Essential minerals
items.content: The fish provides selenium, iodine and phosphorus, important for thyroid health and bone strength.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Although lower than fatty fish, haddock still contributes EPA and DHA omega‑3s that benefit heart health.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to fish, including haddock.

items.title: Mercury content
items.content: Haddock is classified as low‑mercury fish, but excessive consumption should still be balanced with other protein sources.

items.title: Frying oil quality
items.content: High frying temperatures can produce trans fats; use oils with a high smoke point such as canola or sunflower.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Breaded and fried preparations often contain added salt, which may be a concern for people with hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve fried haddock hot, with lemon wedges, tartar sauce, or malt vinegar. It works well in fish tacos, salads, sandwiches, or as a standalone main dish.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked fried haddock in an airtight container in the refrigerator for 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze in a sealed bag at –18 °C, where it retains quality for up to 2 months.
